items.stem: What is the role of Microsoft.Extensions.AI (MEAI) in a .NET application?

options.text: A unified set of C# abstractions (e.g. IChatClient) for interacting with AI services across providers
options.rationale: Correct: MEAI is a provider-neutral abstraction layer for model interaction in .NET.

options.text: A complete multi-step agent orchestration framework
options.rationale: MEAI alone is not an agent framework; agentic orchestration needs more.

options.text: A replacement for dependency injection in .NET
options.rationale: MEAI fits into DI rather than replacing it.

options.text: A proprietary API tied to a single model vendor
options.rationale: MEAI is deliberately a unifying layer, not vendor-specific.

items.explanation: Correct: MEAI is a provider-neutral abstraction layer for model interaction in .NET.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Select TWO situations where a full agent framework (rather than a plain MEAI call) is justified.

options.text: The task requires goal-directed, multi-step orchestration
options.rationale: Correct: multi-step, goal-directed work is where an agent framework earns its complexity.

options.text: The feature must call several tools and decide the sequence dynamically
options.rationale: Correct: dynamic tool selection and sequencing is agentic behavior.

options.text: A single one-shot summarization of a block of text
options.rationale: A one-shot summary is served fine by a plain MEAI call.

options.text: Returning a fixed templated string with no model call
options.rationale: No model call means neither MEAI nor an agent is needed.

options.text: A stateless classification with one prompt
options.rationale: A single-prompt classification does not need agent orchestration.

items.explanation: Correct: multi-step, goal-directed work is where an agent framework earns its complexity.

items.stem: Before shipping an AI feature, which practice best guards against silent quality regressions as prompts and models change?

options.text: Define evaluations that compare outputs and catch regressions
options.rationale: Correct: an evaluation/regression layer catches quality drops as prompts, models and tools evolve.

options.text: Remove all logging to protect privacy
options.rationale: Removing observability makes regressions harder to detect, not easier.

options.text: Hard-code one model version forever and never test
options.rationale: Pinning without testing still misses regressions from prompt or data changes.

options.text: Rely only on the model provider marketing claims
options.rationale: Vendor claims are not a substitute for your own evaluations.

items.explanation: Correct: an evaluation/regression layer catches quality drops as prompts, models and tools evolve.
